coverage_notes: Exhaustive sweep across graph database visualization UX covering: (1) OFFICIAL PRODUCT SOURCES - Neo4j Bloom 2.34, Linkurious Enterprise 4.3+, Kineviz GraphXR 2.17+, Memgraph Lab, Gephi, TigerGraph GraphStudio, Tom Sawyer Perspectives/Explorations, ArangoDB Graph Visualizer, NebulaGraph Studio; (2) ANALYST REPORTS - Gartner Market Guide (T0), Forrester Wave Q4 2020, Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud DBMS, G2/Capterra/TrustRadius review aggregates; (3) MARKET SIZING - MarketsandMarkets/Mordor Intelligence/Knowledge Sourcing data visualization market forecasts 2025-2030 (CAGR 10-15%), graph technology market $5.24B→$18.12B 2025-2034; (4) FOUNDATIONAL HCI - Shneiderman taxonomy/mantra papers (T2), Tamara Munzner visualization textbook (T2), Edward Tufte Visual Display (T2), Don Norman Design of Everyday Things (T2); (5) ACADEMIC - arXiv force-directed layout papers, ACM CHI/UIST interaction design, TOCHI journal, usability studies on visual analytics dashboards; (6) IMPLEMENTATION LIBRARIES - D3.js, Cytoscape.js, KeyLines/ReGraph, yEd, Cambridge Intelligence platform; (7) COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE - 15+ tool comparison articles, Neo4j 15-tool taxonomy, network analysis tools 2025-2026 comparisons. Verified URLs real via WebFetch. Deduped across 50+ raw search results down to 40 high-value sources. Key gap: limited academic papers specifically on graph database viz UX (mostly general InfoVis/IA). Notable authorities: Shneiderman (T2), Munzner (T2), Tufte (T2), Neo4j (T0), Gartner (T0/T2), Cambridge Intelligence (T3 but strong practitioner)

sources.title: Shneiderman's Visual Information-Seeking Mantra
sources.notes: Foundational principle: 'Overview first, zoom and filter, then details-on-demand.' Core visualization design heuristic applicable to graph UX design.

sources.title: Shneiderman (1996): 'The Eyes Have It' - Task by Data Type Taxonomy
sources.notes: Seminal taxonomy: 7 data types, 7 tasks (overview, zoom, filter, details-on-demand, relate, history, extract). Foundational to information visualization design principles applicable to graph visualization.

sources.title: Tamara Munzner: 'Visualization Analysis and Design' Textbook
sources.notes: Comprehensive framework for visualization design: information viz, scientific viz, visual analytics. Covers principles, design choices, interaction techniques applicable to graph visualization UX.

sources.title: Edward Tufte: 'The Visual Display of Quantitative Information' (2nd Ed.)
sources.notes: Landmark design principles: data-ink ratio, graphical deception detection, design excellence. Applicable to graph visualization aesthetic and clarity standards.

sources.title: Don Norman: 'The Design of Everyday Things' (Revised Edition)
sources.notes: Foundational interaction design: signifiers, discoverability, feedback. Principles applicable to graph database UI affordances and interaction patterns.

sources.title: Satyanarayan et al. (UIST 2014): Declarative Interaction Design for Data Visualization
sources.notes: Interaction design principles for visualization: lifting interactions to data level for reusability and expressivity. Applicable to graph exploration workflows.

sources.title: ForceAtlas2: Continuous Graph Layout Algorithm for Gephi
sources.notes: Key layout algorithm used in Gephi and other tools. Physics-based force-directed layout for network visualization of 10-10,000 nodes.

sources.title: arXiv: BatchLayout - Parallel Force-Directed Graph Layout Algorithm
sources.notes: Recent algorithmic work on accelerating force-directed layout via parallelization, relevant to scaling graph visualization for large networks.
